about: build.clang_patches rule `licm-cheap-copies`: machine loop-invariant code motion as LLVM 20 and earlier had it,
counting every copy as a cheap instruction (MachineLICMImpl::IsCheapInstruction: isAsCheapAsAMove or
isCopyLike, that is COPY or SUBREG_TO_REG). LLVM 21 (a38cf8573890, "[MachineLICM] Let targets decide if copy
instructions are cheap") keeps only SUBREG_TO_REG, so a cross-class copy of a loop-invariant value (an AArch64
`fmov s1, w22` of a float constant built in a general register) is no longer cheap and is hoisted out of the
loop, into a callee-saved register when pressure allows; with the older rule it is hoisted only when that adds
no register pressure and otherwise stays in the loop beside its use. No option restores it (hoist-cheap-insts
hoists more, not less), so the rule is a byte patch: IsProfitableToHoist has IsCheapInstruction inlined, and
the edit replaces its compare of the opcode with SUBREG_TO_REG (12) by one that also accepts COPY (20),
`(opcode - 12) & ~8 == 0`, made room for by encoding the instructions around it more compactly. zkit applies a
patch to a copy of the binary whose SHA-256 is the patch's `sha256` (the official release, or the copy
another rule made first), checks each edit's `old` bytes first and the result against `patched_sha256`
(build.patched_clang). Offsets are file offsets; each `why` names the instructions (virtual addresses) it
changes. A macOS copy's ad hoc code signature gets the changed pages' hashes after the edits
(build.refresh_code_signature), so its `patched_sha256` is of the copy with them.

patches.release: LLVM 22.1.8 for Linux x86-64, LLVM-22.1.8-Linux-X64.tar.xz: bin/clang-22 (bin/clang and bin/clang++ link to it)
patches.function: (anonymous namespace)::MachineLICMImpl::IsProfitableToHoist at 0xba2cc40, which has IsCheapInstruction inlined: after TII->isAsCheapAsAMove (the call at 0xba2cc95, CheapInstr set to 1 at 0xba2cc9b) it compares the opcode (MachineInstr+0x44) with SUBREG_TO_REG at 0xba2cca6, then reads the number of defs (MCInstrDesc+4) at 0xba2ccbd for the latency test

edits.why: 0xba2cca6-0xba2ccc5: `cmpw $0xc, 0x44(%rbx); mov %rbx, %r11; mov 0x8(%rsp), %r10; je 0xba2cd96; mov 0x10(%r11), %rax; movzbl 0x4(%rax), %ebx; xor %r9d, %r9d; test %ebx, %ebx` -> `mov %rbx, %r11; mov 0x8(%rsp), %r10; movzwl 0x44(%rbx), %eax; sub $0xc, %eax; and $-9, %eax; je 0xba2ccc6; mov 0x10(%r11), %rax; xor %ebx, %ebx; xor %r9d, %r9d; or 0x4(%rax), %bl`: a COPY or SUBREG_TO_REG reaches the unchanged `je 0xba2cd96` at 0xba2ccc6 with ZF set and CheapInstr still 1 (r9b), as SUBREG_TO_REG did; anything else reads the number of defs into ebx as before and tests it there

MachineLICMImpl::IsProfitableToHoist at 0x1412fa650 (no symbols; found from the hoist-cheap-insts option, whose value it reads at 0x1412fb3ab with CanCauseHighRegPressure inlined, and IsCheapInstruction inlined too): after TII->isAsCheapAsAMove (the call at 0x1412fa7d3, CheapInstr set to 1 at 0x1412fa7d9) it compares the opcode (MachineInstr+0x54) with SUBREG_TO_REG at 0x1412fa7e4, then reads the number of defs (MCInstrDesc+4, the descriptor at MachineInstr+0x18) at 0x1412fa7fb

edits.why: 0x1412fa7e4-0x1412fa809: `cmp word ptr [r12 + 0x54], 0xc; mov r10, [rsp + 0x48]; je 0x1412fa898; mov rax, [r12 + 0x18]; movzx esi, byte ptr [rax + 4]; xor r13d, r13d; test esi, esi; je 0x1412fa898` -> `mov r10, [rsp + 0x48]; mov rax, [r12 + 0x18]; movzx esi, byte ptr [rax + 4]; movzx eax, word ptr [r12 + 0x54]; sub eax, 0xc; and eax, -9; je 0x1412fa805; xor r13d, r13d; test esi, esi; je 0x1412fa882; nop`: a COPY or SUBREG_TO_REG reaches the unchanged `je 0x1412fa898` at 0x1412fa882 with ZF set and CheapInstr still 1 (r13b), as SUBREG_TO_REG did; anything else zeroes r13d and tests the number of defs, which goes there too when it is 0 (rax, esi and the flags are written again before they are read on either path; nothing branches into the range)

edits.why: 0x10128e944-0x10128e95b: `mov x1, x19; blr x8; mov w15, #1; tbnz w0, #0, 0x10128e960; ldrh w8, [x19, #0x44]; cmp w8, #0xc` -> `blr x8; mov w15, #1; tbnz w0, #0, 0x10128e960; ldrh w8, [x19, #0x44]; cmp w8, #0xc; ccmp w8, #0x14, #4, ne`: x1 still holds the instruction from the function's entry (x19 is its copy, and nothing branches into 0x10128e930-0x10128e95f), so the move before the call makes room for the compare with COPY; the unchanged `b.ne 0x10128ef5c` at 0x10128e95c goes to the number-of-defs test only for neither opcode
